title: CRISPR Screening Identifies Mechanisms of Resistance to KRASG12C and SHP2 Inhibitor Combinations in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
model: KRAS-G12C-mutant NSCLC lines (NCI-H23 analyzed), genome-wide knockout library (18,360 genes, 3 EPIC pools)
contrast: KRASG12C+SHP2 inhibitor combination vs DMSO, NCI-H23 (1 vs 1, no replicates)
paper_method: RSA (Dafflon procedure) per cell line; gene scores in geneData.txt.gz
paper_calls: FGFR1 strongest sensitizer and PTEN strongest rescuer (panel-wide); heparan-sulfate genes (B4GALT7, EXT1/2, EXTL3) sensitize; NF1, YAP1, KEAP1, MED12, CIC rescue; validated FGFR dependence
barcs_calls: Rescuers (enriched): PTEN #1, PLCG1 #2, NF1 #3, ARIH2 #4, CUL5 #6, KEAP1 #63 of 18,907; sensitizers (depleted): EXTL3 #235, ITGB1 #303, EXT1/EXT2/B4GALT7 significant, FGFR1 #4399 (panel-wide hit, mid-pack in this line); ranking reliable, FDR count uncalibrated (n=1, 10 controls)
named_hits: rescuers recovered at top (PTEN #1, NF1 #3, CUL5 #6, ARIH2 #4, matching the paper's own NCI-H23 RSA); heparan-sulfate sensitizers recovered; FGFR1 mid-pack in NCI-H23
verdict: Raw per-library counts recovered from the long-format deposit; in NCI-H23 BARCS reproduces the paper's own RSA rescuer ranking almost exactly (PTEN #1, plus PLCG1/NF1/ARIH2/CUL5) and recovers the heparan-sulfate sensitizers, while FGFR1 ranks mid-pack because it is a panel-wide not per-line hit; rescuer agreement strong, sensitizer agreement partial, FDR count uncalibrated at n=1.
